And it's possible that some people used that term. However, there was a Territorial Defence staff in Kozarac. The fact that it was broadened in this emergency situation means that it was expanded. It means that it dealt with the crisis, but it was not a Crisis Staff. It was a Territorial Defence staff. That's what I know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, to the best of your knowledge, who the members of that group were, or entity, as you've described it? Who were some of the members?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the Territorial Defence and there was a commander of the Territorial Defence. There was the police as well, and the chief of police. There was also the reserve police force or the so-called war police. All in accordance with the existing laws. There was an individual who was the head of the structure. There was also the civilian protection which also had a chief. There was the local commune and the president of the local commune. All these individuals made up a body which discussed the issue of defence in cases of -- in case of an attack on the surrounding villages. The central body, the one that was competent and had authority in the organisational sense, was actually the Territorial Defence staff, that is, the command of the Territorial Defence or the commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you list for me, sir, the names of those individuals?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Osmaj, Osman, was with the police. I further know that there was a person who was the head of the local government office. Then there was Mr. Becir Medunjanin, who was there from the municipal secretariat for national defence. I cannot remember any other names.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Causevic was a member?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Causevic. What was his name? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's all I have, just his last name. How about Mr. Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bahonjic, Islam Bahonjic was from the Kamicani local commune. It's possible that he had some kind of post in Kamicani but I'm not sure about that. I know that he, Islam Bahonjic, went to Prijedor to take part in negotiations there. But he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about an individual by the name of Mr. Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, with the Court's permission, have the usher tender a document to the witness, and we have copies for the Court. And the first one, we would ask it be given to the OTP. We would provisionally ask that it be marked or identified as Exhibit D13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. Provision D13, and we remain with D12, that there will be no decision on the admission into evidence today until the dispute is settled.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, just let me know when you've had an opportunity to review the document so I may put some questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read all of it, but I have looked at the first, the second, the third, and the fourth page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what it is. I can see that it's handwritten and could, perhaps, be some kind of minutes of a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what's the date of that meeting? 26th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, 26th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, because I forgot a question with respect to the prior issue. Who from your area, from the local commune of Trnopolje, was a member of the Crisis Staff or the Territorial Defence that you previously described and the individuals that were included in there? Who from Trnopolje specifically was on that committee?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. In terms of function, no, I know a few individuals. If I saw a photograph, I'm sure I would be able to recognise a few members of the Territorial Defence. As to who had authority, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the first page of the B/C/S document dated 26/4/1992, it has on the third word "RK" and "S." Do you know what that stands for, sir, "RKS"? Is it the republic Crisis Staff, the regional Crisis Staff, or the Hratne War Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it stands for any of the three possibilities that you enumerated. I think it could actually mean the regional Crisis Staff, "rajon." Because the Territorial Defence is divided into departments, the so-called rajoni. The department or the area of Kamicani, the area of Kozarusa, the area of Trnopolje, and I think that the "RKS" stands for Rejonski Krizni Stab, Area Crisis Staff. That's how it would translate, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In what area in particular are we, then, speaking of, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking in general terms. The Territorial Defence was divided into areas, notwithstanding the region. I don't see anything in particular here. It just says the work of the RKS, from the last meeting until today. Mention is made of Kozarac and a number of villages in the area of Kozarac. So the area in question obviously is Kozarac or the surrounding villages. I can see Hadzici. No, excuse me, these must be the names, the surnames, of the people here. I am familiar with some of these individuals and I know that they come from Kozarac or the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In fact, on the item under "agenda," it identifies Kozarac, Trnopolje, and several other areas. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Under --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under point 1, Kozarusa, Kozarac, Trnopolje, Kevljani, Kamicani. Underneath, it says "Kozarusa, not organised." Underneath Kozarac, we read the word "organisation." An additional text is written below these other names. "Conflict," I don't know exactly what it means. And this is actually an enumeration of the local communes in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Knowing the individuals that appear on this document, sir, do you know what role they played with respect to the Crisis Staff that is referenced in this document?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we read the surname of Bahonjic. I knew Islam Bahonjic, who was a deputy at the Municipal Assembly and lived in the area of Kamicani. Whether he had a function at the Territorial Defence, I don't know. But I know him from the municipal parliament sessions. I can further see the surname of Causevic, but I don't know who the individual is. It goes on with the surname of Hadzic. The individual in question is possibly Mr. Hadzic from the village of Hadzici, who was also a deputy at the Municipal Assembly and was also an official with the local party branch. Hadzic, it says, a proposal, a suggestion, is being made that the few of us should go there and try to exert influence and so on and so forth. I believe that his name was Teufik, but I'm not a hundred per cent sure. But it would be logical because Bahonjic is here, so it was only logical that Hadzic was present as well. However, I don't know about Causevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Under Mr. Hadzic's name, it talks about an issue of food provisions for daytime checkpoints. Do you see that in the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it talks about the food provision for the checkpoints in Dera and Krkici. Below, we read again the name of Bahonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where were those two checkpoints in relation to either Kozarac or the town of Prijedor, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to Kozarac, it says here Dera and Krkici. I know that Dera is village situated right above the town of Kozarac, going in the direction of Kozarusa. The village is situated along a creek. The area of Krkici refers to the lower part of Kozarac, below the Prijedor/Banja Luka Road. I don't know exactly what part of Krkici or what Krkici they had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Directing your attention to page 2 of the B/C/S document, sir, it continues to talk about Mr. Bahonjic, and then it lists certain weapons. Can you please read for us what is said on page 2 of the B/C/S document which can be found, for the Court, on page 1 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below the upper text, we see a list consisting of several items concerning weapons. Under point 1, that is, in the first row, the number I think is 7, Zoljas, handheld rocket launchers - 2, "KAM." I don't know what it is. It must be the abbreviations of the names of villages around Kozarac, and the -- in the abbreviation of the town of Kozarac itself. 2 Kamicani, 1 Kevljani, the abbreviation, that is, and 1 Kozar -- I don't know whether this stands for Kozarusa, but most probably it does. Underneath, we read: "One TROMB," probably an abbreviation for "tromblom." 2 DP, AP, which is an abbreviation for an automatic rifle. And then the number of the rifle in question. And the location of Kevljani - 30 pieces of ammunition. It goes on. One automatic rifle, and the number of the rifle. Trnopolje, 30 pieces of ammunition. Next row: 2 PAP, which is an abbreviation for a semi automatic rifle, "dash" one PAP for Kozarusa, followed by the number of the rifle in question, one semi automatic rifle to go to Kozarac. Yes, that's what it says, to send to Kozarac. And then we read the letters KOZE or KOLE. I don't know what it means. "Three clips of ammunition for Kevljani and Trnopolje" is written underneath. The next row reads: "One bomb,, Kamicani, one grenade." Then we have an illegible part -- Kozarac. One sniper, Besici. The next row reads: "Two Zoljas, Hrnici; two Zoljas, Suhi Brod; and two Zoljas, Dera." These are the villages in the area of Kozarac. The next row, "One semi automatic rifle, Kozarac 1," that is the local commune of Kozarac because the town itself was divided in several local communes. "One semi automatic rifle, Kozarac 2." It goes on ": One Zolja, one hand grenade, one clip, Kozarac 2." Underneath, "One semi automatic rifle, Kamicani." That is what I can read on this piece of paper I have translated or rather explained to you the abbreviations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And just a further explanation, did you mention the one sniper that's listed in the middle section of that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read loud and clear all of the rows of this text. It says: "One sniper" but no further description is given. We don't know if it's a hunting sniper or a military sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the second line of that description of weapons, there's the word that you described as a "TROMB." Can you describe for me as a person who was in the reserve and who was specifically in the artillery unit of the reserve, the military reserve of the JNA, what is that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said TROMB. It says here -- it reads "TROMB." So it must be an abbreviation. And I said that it was my assumption that the abbreviation stood for tromblom. It was customary for all military-age men to have it. It's a sort of extension for an ordinary type of rifle, which is used in case of the attack of armoured vehicles, something that all military age men were familiar with and had undergone training in. I also think that the Territorial Defence had a specific number of trombloms, which is actually a rifle-launched grenade. They each had a few pieces of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From your experience, sir, this rifle-launched grenade, that is a weapon that can cripple and, in fact, destroy tanks. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot destroy a tank, no. It is a very light type of weapon. Not even Zoljas, the hand-held rocket launchers that are listed here can destroy a tank. Different weapons are used for the purposes of destroying tanks. As far as I can remember, these rifle-launched grenades or trombloms, every squad or every platoon had a number of individuals who carried such rifle-launched grenades. I don't know exactly about their use, but they were not used against large armoured vehicles. Perhaps to attack armoured personnel carriers or bunkers, I'm not sure. I'm not an expert in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to the individual that's identified there as Kole, do you know if that is a member who was also a member of a paramilitary group that operated in the Prijedor Municipality in 1992, otherwise known as Kolina's group?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of the individual by the name of Kole. As regards paramilitary units, I don't know. But as far as I remember, there were no paramilitary units as such. I know that the Territorial Defence had mobilised all of those who had placed themselves at the disposal of the Territorial Defence and who had any -- some kind of weapon, even the people who did not have any weapons but wished to participate in the defence. Well, how these individuals referred to themselves, I don't know. How they called themselves, that's a different problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why do you see it as a problem as to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why do you see it, sir, as a problem as to how these individuals identified and called themselves during the period April through May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I may have used the wrong word. I should have said it's a completely different issue because there were a number of individuals who identified themselves with various names, as the yellows, the greens, the reds, I don't know. It is typical for every army. I'm only talking about the Territorial Defence and those who were outside the framework of the Territorial Defence. I mean, had there been such elements, I would have known about them, had there been units who did not wish to be organised in the Territorial Defence. We were actually afraid that such cases would happen and cause incidents which would then serve as a pretext for an attempt by the Serbian artillery or infantry. That was the very purpose of organising this defence. There were no paramilitary units or formations whatsoever. And I am sure that I would have been aware of that had such units existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the incidents that you were afraid of having been made by various groups, are the incidents those that did, in fact, occur, the incident at Hambarine, the incident at Kozarac, in the period that we discussed earlier today? Are those the type of incidents that you were afraid that paramilitary groups would actually provoke and then, unfortunately, a response by the military would follow? Are those the incidents?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think we understand each other, or you may have misinterpreted and abused what I have said. But it's possible that there has been a misunderstanding. Great care was taken of the demands of the population that a defence be organised through the existing bodies of the Territorial Defence in case of an attack. And from the very beginning, any possibility for having people, individuals, working outside this legal framework was eliminated. We tried not to create conditions for such a phenomenon to occur. And one of the main reasons why we paid attention to that was the fact that the members of the Territorial Defence tried to exert as much influence and control over their individuals in order to prevent individuals from making various types of provocations in, say, a drunken state. This has nothing to do with the incident which occurred at Hambarine or in -- on the Prijedor/Banja Luka Road as it was claimed by the Serbian Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about this paramilitary group that we've gotten some evidence on and see if you know them. How about Ramiz's group? Are you familiar with a group called Ramiz's group?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know a group by the name of Didin's group?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have only heard of an individual called Didin. He was actually called Hasan, but they called him Didin. He was killed. And I repeat, Kole himself was a member of a Territorial Defence unit. And it is possible that he referred to his unit as "my unit" or "Kole's group." It is also possible that outsiders referred to this group as "Kole's group." But this group was part of the Territorial Defence. Similarly, later with the military, you had "Cobras" or "Wolves" or units that had named themselves according to the names of their commanders. This was something -- this was different. All I'm trying to say was that nothing was done outside the control of the Territorial Defence. I mean, I was involved enough to have been able to notice such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about the Green Berets, sir? Were they considered a paramilitary group in April 1992? Or is it your opinion that they also were only part of the Territorial Defence under the command of the Territorial Defence of Kozarac? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have to repeat once again: The formation of Green Berets never existed in the territory of the Prijedor municipality. The fact that certain individuals referred to themselves as such is a different issue. Generally speaking, at the level of the republic -- do you want to hear me? So at the level of the republic, or in the media, we had already heard about a unit which was called the Green Berets in Sarajevo. It was probably a response to the Red Berets, that is, the special military forces that had come to Bosnia from Serbia in several waves. So there was a group which referred to themselves prior to the establishment of the BH army as the "Green Berets." Later, after the army had been set up, there were no Green Berets whatsoever. I even think that the members of this group, the Green Berets, later on had lots of problems with the military administration. The main staff of the Territorial Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please slow down a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And repeat the last portion of your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the last portion of your answer wasn't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. You want me to repeat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The individuals who referred to themselves as Green Berets in the town of Sarajevo were never part of the establishment, according to the decisions issued by the government organs, at least in Sarajevo. So it was not a decision made by the Territorial Defence or any other body. This was a group that called itself that, but according to the establishment, they were part of the Territorial Defence of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As for Prijedor, at the local level, for example, in Trnopolje, there was not a single man bearing arms known as a member of the Green Berets. I'm also speaking of Kozarac. So the people who put themselves at the disposal of the Territorial Defence were not called that. I don't know if there were such units elsewhere, but I repeat, such a formation was never established either at the municipal or the republic level. And because I'm speaking fast, I will repeat: In the town of Sarajevo, the Green Berets had a lot of complications with the administration when they wanted to register the fact that they were a part of the armed forces at the beginning of the war, when the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was being set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I agree with your earlier comment that we maybe don't understand each other, and it's possibly that it's my fault. I'm not interested to know if these paramilitary groups, Kolina's, Ramiz's, Didin's, the Green Berets, or any other others that may have existed, whether they existed legally or legitimately. All I want to know from you, sir, is whether or not those paramilitary groups existed in the area of Prijedor Municipality from April through May of 1992. I agree with you that they weren't legal entities, but did they exist?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I heard about this as much as you did. I heard that some people called a unit commanded by Kole "Kole's group." Of course, I heard in the Territorial Defence that there were no groups outside the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you hear, sir, if the mujahedin were fighting in Bosnia at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time. I learned about this from the press a few years later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you learn from the press that, in fact, they were in the Bosnia area in the spring of 1992? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember having read that, not about that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the article that you read, sir, did that tell you how it came about that they were present in Bosnia and under whose command did they come under?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some foreign soldiers who decided to fight on the side of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as far as I know from the press, arrived, first as members of humanitarian organisations. Later on, they volunteered to join the armed struggle. Most of them were from Islamic countries, but there were also some Britons, some Germans. I don't know about other nationalities, but I do know about the ones I've mentioned. I read that, later on, they established their own unit, but I know nothing about the details. I can only tell you my impression of what I read in the paper, so I'm not a good source for that sort of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this: Which source or which press report did you refer to earlier?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first, the Serbian television spoke a lot about it, then various newspapers in Sarajevo, the independent press. Also, papers that supported one or other of the political parties. This was also something that international bodies investigated, and these people were interviewed. I was not especially interested in this so I did not go into it any further. I concentrated on my duties. That is why this is something I never investigated. I'm just trying to tell you what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the duties that you continued to do was the duties, actually, as the representative of the chamber of municipalities in the Prijedor Municipality? Are those the duties you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to 1995 or early 1996. Today, I have nothing to do with politics or any political party and this has been the case for some time. And I have not kept up with political events.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me try to move along with some other documents I'd like to ask you about it. Do you know if on October 24th, 1991, at an SDA party meeting, that certain members were assigned weapons duties? That is, again, October 24th, 1991. Do you recall any such meeting or anything like that occurring?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember any meetings from that period. I don't remember, but I do know that in that period, as a response to the behaviour and the moves of the SDS, all possibilities were discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it your general testimony, just so I get it right, because you mentioned Red Berets and the Green Berets, the Bosnian Muslims, all they did was essentially respond, and whatever they did, it was essentially a response to what the SDS did. Is that basically what your testimony, in a nutshell, is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we've spoken about a lot of things. For the most part, yes, but we would have to go over it again to establish whether it refers to everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're keeping track and we'll get to that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may have the Court instruct the usher to assist me with the next exhibit, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's my understanding that you tendered the document with the provisional number D13. Are there objections by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I've now lost track of documents. You mean this one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then admitted into evidence D13 A, English; D13 B, B/C/S. Please, may I ask, for a better understanding, this document was disclosed by the OTP and translated by the OTP before disclosure. Right? Can you identify it from the bottom line?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At the moment, we can't identify where this comes from. It has got no ERN numbers on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, my question is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But we think it was part of the TO documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you assist us with this, for a better understanding, that you can mark it on the list of exhibits what it is? We are still discussing D13.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can get back to the Court on that - I do not have the exact binder of which this document was found - but it's my recollection that it's from a binder of documents, and I'll be able to provide the Court with the specific answer on that, that was provided to us from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Because I'm a little bit surprised, to be honest, about the bottom line indicating the document number. To a certain extent, it differs from others. Maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we think, whatever this is, it's not an official translation. We think we know when we disclosed, but we're not at all sure where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Whatever it may be, with the assistance of the witness before us, we got some access to the content of this document. Thank you. Then the next would be provisional D14.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would ask the Court, because we're unclear, this may be J3, but I'm not -- I don't know. For some reason, our notes seem to reflect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it's J3 -- with The Hague the 20th of November, 1991. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would like then for the witness to be shown J3, because I have a couple questions on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And sorry, registry, it's not D14. It's indeed already admitted under J3.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can have the usher remove the other documents in front of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I have some legal problems. Using a document which - I have to be cautious - which may be forgery, using such a document in the courtroom, knowing that it's a forgery, may cause problems even for Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to be heard on this briefly, and I'm glad the Court pointed it out, which is why initially, quite frankly, as the Court remembers that was a document that we were going to introduce and withdrew it, and then -- for the same reason, and then the Court ask that it be introduced. I think it's important, though, that we perhaps touch on this outside the presence of the witness because I think we may be able to clarify the issue that the Court is inquiring about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But please, don't forget that it was admitted into evidence, if not for other purposes, then for the purpose to prove that there is a forgery on the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would ask that the Court, respectfully -- would that opinion, respectfully, be reserved until we are able to at least discuss it, since it was a document that was provided to us by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Shall I proceed with this witness, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you describe Document J3 for us, please. What is it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see before me that this is a photocopy of a manuscript. The date at the top is the 24th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, is it also relating to the SDA meeting wherein certain individuals in certain areas were assigned to weapons duty?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know there are lots of duties assigned here. Where do you see weapons duty?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just reading the English translation, but I'm asking the first line on the first page of the B/C/S version under the date of 24/10/1991. Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask for a short break, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. --- Break taken at 1.17 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. We just conferred in depth, and therefore we thought it would be better to do it outside with the assistance of an interpreter. No, the Bench will now at allow to proceed on the basis of a document which, to be very diplomatic, where this is at least a strong suspicion that it's a forgery and we can't allow to use forgery as a basis of a witness statement in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we suddenly worked out where these documents come from, why they are in this form. They were provided to the OTP as part of the Tadic case. They come from the Tadic Defence lawyers. Your Honour, I don't know one way or the other, but I have looked, and I've looked at the transcript of what was said, and I have to say I think Mr. Koumjian may have slightly misinterpreted the 20th of November entry which led everybody to believe that it may be a forgery. I don't know one way or the other. The simplest way, of course, is to establish from the Tadic Defence lawyers where these documents come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just ask a couple questions, not on the document - we have your ruling - but in connection with that specific issue in a general sense to the witness, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But please, not on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course. May the usher be asked to remove the document from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, as a member of the republican assembly, were you aware of a conference, the European Conference on Security and Cooperation involving the Serbian and Bosnian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991? Are you aware of that organisation?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This organisation did exist but not in connection with the Serbs and Muslims in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's an organisation that has always existed and still exists today. A few days earlier, when you asked me the same question, of course I knew because their delegates, the delegates, of the OSCE monitored the parliament sessions. They wore white uniforms. They drove white cars. We referred to them as monitors, or they referred to themselves as such when they held press conferences. I also know in principle - and I repeat in principle - what their function was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. And their involvement was from approximately June of 1991 through when?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but they were there until the attack on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Sarajevo started. I think they were at the last assembly meeting that I attended in Sarajevo, but I can't be quite sure. I think they were there throughout that period until the situation deteriorated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There was also an entity from the European community, correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The European community and the capes [as interpreted] were there, so were the ambassadors of foreign countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was the UN there at all, or any representatives from the UN?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure. I know that, later on, they were present in large numbers, but I don't know whether they were there then.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if on July 5th, 1991, the European community issued a declaration with respect to the situation in the former Yugoslavia, namely, in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Are you familiar with that decision or declaration?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the international community dealt with the status of the various republics of the former Yugoslavia extensively and the pretensions of Serbia Montenegro toward other republics. I know the international organised a number of conferences and negotiations. But as for the exact chronological order and what meetings were held, I don't remember that. But I can tell you that the international community was very involved in all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where they met initially when they would discuss these issues? Do you know where in Europe they met?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Europe?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where? They met here at The Hague, didn't they, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I find this question rather funny. I don't know that they met in The Hague. I know that they met in Skopje in Macedonia, and in Lisbon later on. I don't know whether this was 1992 or 1993. I know that there were several international conferences, but this was at the higher political level, so I wouldn't know a lot about that. I paid attention to what my job was and the work of the parliament in Sarajevo. From time to time, we did receive reports from various international gatherings, but I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may now ask the Court to have the usher assist me with another document that was provided to us on May 28th, 2002. It's under tab number, I believe, 881. And I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This should be provisional D14. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just quickly, Mr. Sejmenovic, if I can direct your attention to the top right-hand corner of the B/C/S version, number 388. I'll be asking you some questions on that and other documents. But initially, that one.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am looking at page 388.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, what this document is? It's provisionally marked D14.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that these are minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us the date of those minutes?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the "30th of March, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And below, there's four individuals' names which purport to have also their signatures next to their names. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know any of these four individuals?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know them all by sight, and one of them was a friend of mine. He was a secretary in the party, an official secretary employed as such by the party, and he was in charge of the finances for a while, and later on another person was appointed. This refers to Mr. Izet Kararic. And as for the others, I know Evledin, Skapor Salih and Hopovac by sight. Hopovac was on the Executive Board of the party. It's possible that Kadiric was also, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signatures of any of those individuals, including the individual of Mr. Kadiric?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some signatures here, but I don't know what their signatures look like, so I can neither confirm nor deny that these are their signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, within that document below, in the centre of the document, it makes reference that certain money was given to a Crisis Staff. Do you see that? There's 8.000 din, and then it goes on. Talking about a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just interrupt for a better understanding because, once again, we are surprised to read on the first page a stamp "SDA," north Rhine Westphalia, which is north Rhine Westphalia in Germany. It's a document from Germany, is it right?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to get back to that. There are some documents here that apparently were from the -- and I don't want to give testimony - from an SDA entity abroad where monies were collected for whatever reason, trying to remain neutral, yes. I'm going to ask him about that, but I wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just for a better understanding, were these documents attached to each other? That would mean that, for example, here the first page, you tendered "SDS, north Rhine Westphalia," and then the town of Essen, that this collection was done in Germany or is it an misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's a misunderstanding. But to answer the Court's question, we were given the 18 pages that were provided to the Court in exactly the same format that we have tendered it in. In fact, I have the copy of the letter which corresponds to that which indicates that there are ten English pages and eight B/C/S pages. So all we did was not give the Court the communication between the OTP and the Defence. But that is how we got the document on May 28th, 2002, which the OTP states may fall within Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedures and Evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may continue, Your Honour. Would the Court mind if I just have an answer to my question, and then I'll get back to the stamp. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to page 388 of the B/C/S version of this document wherein you identified certain individuals that you knew professionally and personally, it mentions, I believe, on at least three occasions a Crisis Staff. And again, the letter we're referring to, or the minutes we're referring to, are dated 3 -- meaning March 30th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here, the Crisis Staff. I'm waiting for your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to know if you saw it or not. Did you see it in there? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What Crisis Staff, on March 30th, 1992, in Prijedor would these four individuals be referring to if, according to you, none existed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you several times that the Crisis Staff, formally speaking, was never established, formally, that a body should be established named the Crisis Staff, that it should have its stamp and the president and so on and so forth. How these groups of people were commonly referred to and how these individuals were called in light of their functions, I don't know. I think that this is some kind of financial report of this body. It says here it is distributed to the Crisis Staff, but it doesn't say which Crisis Staff. I don't know about any specific body of this kind at the time, nor have I ever seen a document which would have been signed as a document of a Crisis Staff. I think it was the Territorial Defence and the Territorial Defence staff. Again, that's just my opinion. It's not necessarily correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were any of these four individuals that are identified which bear their signature on that page 388, were they members of the Territorial Defence in Kozarac or in any other area on or about March 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you can just -- if I may direct your attention to the second page of that document which bears the number 390 on the top right-hand corner, and can you tell me if you know anything about this stamp which seems to be from the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see a stamp of this kind. I know. I can read "SDA." Underneath, we read "Nordrhein Westfalen demokratisch acktion." And underneath, it reads: "The party for democratic action." So it is possible that this is the stamp of the SDA branch in Germany established in this town and in this region. According to what it says in the stamp, that would be it. But I don't know whether that is the case. I know that the SDA, as well as the majority of the parties that were created in the area of the former Yugoslavia, had its branches in -- abroad, the SDA, the HDZ, the Slovenian parties and the political parties from other republics. I've just told you what I see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Quickly, if I may direct your attention to page 385 which appears on the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found 385.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It also identifies three of the same individuals which appeared on the March 30th, 1992 document, correct, that you've discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it also identifies Dr. Mirza Mujadzic, do you see his name at the bottom, the signature that appears to be his to the right of his name?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise Dr. Mujadzic's signature at all, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I never paid attention to signatures. I know that the three named individuals here are the secretary of the Executive Board of the SDA, the treasurer of the SDA, of the Executive Board of the SDA, and Salih Skapur, who was maybe a member of the Executive Board, but I'm not sure. I know that these individuals were in charge of the finances of the party, including the payment of utility costs and similar. It was a normal procedure of obtaining funds for the party, as was done by all other parties, and as it is customarily done by the parties in your country. So we were not an exception in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that these members, as well as other members of the SDA, actually called for a boycott of the work and called for a boycott of the schools and the payment of duties to the Prijedor Municipality on or about April of 1992? That the SDA made that call for a boycott, is that true?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A call to boycott schools and jobs?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about this. I couldn't possibly imagine any political party as having this type of influence over people, that it should appeal to people to give up their salaries without which it would have been impossible for them to live. They were in a difficult situation anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, sir, to page 348 of the documents that you have before you provisionally identified as D14. And it's towards the end. Are you there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at it. 348.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, in the limited time we have, what is on the top left-hand side of that document?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The top left-hand side, on this copy, we see in the upper left corner three letters, "SDA." Underneath: "The Sarajevo party for Democratic Action, regional board for the Banja Luka/Prijedor region." There's no date. There's no stamp. On this paper, which is a memo, a handwritten text can be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Hopefully when we get the original, we'll find the date of that document, sir, but thank you for that. I recognise it doesn't have a date. That document was given to us by the Office of the Prosecutor. Quite frankly, sir, does it not say within this document that has the letterhead of the SDA that there was a call for a boycott for both the work, school, and the payment of duties?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's complete nonsense, sir. How can you ask a question like this? No, never, at any point in time did anyone call for a boycott on behalf of the SDA. Even after the blockade of Kozarac, people still went to work and to school. Up until that moment when they were actually physically turned back and had to stop working --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... This document also was submitted as part of the Tadic original appeal by Tadic's then lawyer. We have no originals. These are the only copies we were provided with. We have no idea where these documents come from, what validity or not they have, whether or not they are genuine. I should say that I am informed that when the -- when Tadic retained new counsel, these documents were not resubmitted as part of the appeal. Your Honour, at the moment, I would object to it being entered into evidence at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think it's quite ironic that the OTP will, two weeks before this witness testifies, give us 18 pages and acknowledge and admit that it forms and is part of the Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, not tell us that the document comes from any suspect sources, invite us to ask questions on it as they did earlier, and then now withdraw it. I'm not sure if we can rely on any of the documents, quite frankly, that the OTP is proposing to us that are undated and unsigned, in light of what they are currently telling us and the position they currently have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a difference between those that we seize as part of a search and seizure operation from various places and those that are supplied to us. We are obliged by the rules to give to the Defence anything which might be Rule 68. I wasn't aware where these documents came from. I don't know whether Dr. Mujadzic was asked about his signature rather than this witness being asked about it. I'm told not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because unfortunately, we were given this on May 28th, 2002, Your Honour. That's when we were given these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's correct to understand that evidently it was translated by the Defence at such time in Tadic, and we can find in the English version on the bottom line "voluntary contributions Essen.Doc/JTR." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll double check, but I think so. I think it was translated by the Tadic -- it doesn't look like one of our references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think, once again, may I ask the parties to go in some more details. Evidently, the OTP followed on the obligation under Rule 68, provided this document, not going into some details, and the Defence is now confronted with a problem whether or not, or where, at least, the source of this document is. Could you please be so kind and provide us with an explanation on the source of this document until tomorrow -- no, not tomorrow, until Wednesday, because we have -- we can only continue on Wednesday with the cross-examination of the witness before us. If not tomorrow, we can finalise the next witness. I don't know whether protect -- no, the next witness, and then we can proceed possibly already tomorrow. But we should know some more information on both documents disputed in present before we decide on the admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll make what inquiries we can. Your Honour, may I just ask: Is this witness's evidence going to be completed on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm confident that we will be able to, Your Honour, but it all depends on the answers provided. But I'm confident that we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And it depends on the number of questions to be put by the Judges. But what is the background of your question, the next witness arriving Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness. And this witness has been here for a very long time. I know Your Honour will say it was four days and 90 minutes in chief, but that was because of the reading of documents into evidence, and Your Honour, I'm not sure it was that. But I think it would be nice if the witness could know whether or not he's going to be leaving here. He has been here for some ten days now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The only thing we can say is we shall try our best, but we can't really conscientiously promise to do so. Unfortunately, we have to leave it open. Of course, it depends when we can start tomorrow. This concludes the day and the trial stands adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 1.48 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of June, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
